Non-finite `now`, non-finite `Date.parse(marker.at)`, non-finite `age`, and now negative `age` all return `null`, and every ambiguous case fails closed (blocked + exit 2), never fail-open to clear. Multi-marker behavior is also conservative: `youngestAt` is `Math.max` over all markers, so one future-dated marker among otherwise-old markers poisons the whole set to `null` — over-conservative, but in the safe direction.\\n\\n(2) The direct `runVerification()` test is genuinely independent — it acquires a lock via `acquireDraftLock(..., { disableHeartbeat: true })` and calls the exported `runVerification()` directly with `{ explicit: true }`, asserting the returned `clear === false` / `inconclusive === true` and the persisted audit `reason`, none of which the `unfreeze`-routed tests can reach (the gate never calls `runVerification`). It is not duplicate coverage. Its limitation is the input choice, per materialDissent.\\n\\n(3) The '9 tests' explanation is correct and sufficient. `node --test <files>` runs each file in its own subprocess and counts one top-level test per FILE; subtests roll up inside the file result and are not flattened into the summary. The isolated run (`tests: 1` for a file containing 57 `test()` blocks) is a clean demonstration of exactly that, and the 3.56s duration for that single 'test' corroborates that the file's body actually executed. EXIT.DUPLICATE : gate.reason === 'index-lag' ?
